issues.title: Fertiliser type for Apr/May 2026 differs
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 10 and Agro 1/2026 Table 5 list Mixture C in April and May (170.20 t, 55.35 t) and Agro photos show Mix C application, but the Agro 1/2026 revised 2026 programme (Appendix 1) and the original 2026 programme (Agro 2/2025 Appendix 1) prescribe only Mix B and RP. Agro Table 5 2nd half also shows Aug RP and Oct/Nov Mix C while Appendix 1 has Jul and Oct Mix B with no RP. Agro 1/2026 says the H2 programme was revised but the Appendix doses are identical to the original.

issues.title: Harvester numbers differ
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 (Apr 2026): 40 harvesters vs 44 required (-4), ratio 1:22 ha; mechanisation table 34 harvesters (7+27). Agro 1/2026 (May 2026): 48 harvesters, a surplus of four, ratio 1:18 ha; mechanisation 36 workers (8+28).

issues.title: Pruning progress inconsistent in Agro
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 9 shows 683.55 of 886.80 ha pruned (balance 203.25 ha) as at March 2026, but text 4.2.2 says round 1 was completed on 100% of the estate by March. PA 1/2026 Table 15 shows 886.80 ha done to April; PA intro says progressive pruning in 'about 0%' of tall palm area delayed while section 6.8.1 says about 10%.

issues.title: Circle weeding progress
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Tables 7–8: round 1 circle and selective spraying completed in all fields (886.80 ha) to April. Agro 1/2026 Table 11: circle round 1 71% as at March, and text 4.4.3 says circle weeding stood at 54% as at April (lower than its own March figure).

issues.title: 2026 Jan–Mar yield 5.23 vs 5.34 t/ha
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 Table 16 gives estate Jan–Mar 2026 as 5.23 t/ha (+11.11%), but Appendix 2(a) gives 4,732.85 t = 5.34 t/ha. Table 16 P05B 2025 printed as 44.43 t/ha (should be about 4.43). Monthly Jan–Mar 2026 (2,034.50 + 1,360.05 + 1,338.0) sum to 4,732.55, not the printed 4,732.85.

issues.title: 2025 tonnage typo
issues.detail: Agro 1/2026 4.1.1 states 2025 production 21,774.29 t exceeding the estimate by 1,774.95 t; Appendix 2(b), Appendix 2(a) and PA 1/2026 Table 19 give 21,774.95 t (20,000 + 1,774.95).

issues.title: Rainfall records disagree
issues.detail: 2025 total printed 4,407 mm (140 days) in both PA 1/2026 App 1 and Agro 1/2026 App 3, but PA months sum to 3,331 mm (Jul 146, Nov 128, Dec 140) and Agro months to 4,307 mm (Jul 46, Nov 745, Dec 599). PA 2023 July printed 1,285.5 mm vs Agro 128.50. Agro 2/2025 App 4 shows entirely different 2021–2023 figures (e.g. 2022 2,781.50 mm vs 4,007.50 in Agro 1/2026); its 2023 column (2,805.80 mm, 137 days) is identical month by month to Sungai Gayung 2022 in Gayung PA 1/2026, so it looks copied from another estate.

issues.title: General charges appendix vs table
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 5 general charges RM445,908.27 (budget RM584,048.00) vs Appendix 2 grand total RM445,739.81 (budget RM583,216.00); management sub-total 171,585.27 vs 171,415.27. Management sub-total lines add to 171,563.39 (actual) and 178,012.00 (budget), not the printed 171,415.27 / 191,012.00. Text 5.2.7 gives water–labour as RM32.31/ha, the same figure as executive salaries (appendix implies about RM8.70/ha); 5.2.2 prints RM54.471.

issues.title: Small table errors in PA 1/2026

issues.title: Trap checks
issues.detail: PA 1/2026 Table 19 'Actual same period' 2025 (5,760.75 t) is a real actual, matching Agro 1/2025 Appendix 2(a) Jan–Apr 2025; '12 months' 21,774.95 t is a full Jan–Dec 2025 total matching Agro monthly records. PA 2/2025 'last year same period' 17,045.74 t equals Jan–Oct 2024 monthly sum. No combined-estate figures. Agro 2/2025 Appendix 3(b) 2025 total 16,984.05 is Jan–Oct only (not used as a year).

actions.item: Check herbicide dosage and spraying technique; premix spraying solution under the supervisor
Palm circle / base raking to clear cut frond butts and debris for loose fruit collection
Spot-spray or poison sporadic jungle woodies and half-dead Clidemia; field check 2 weeks after spraying
Expedite fertiliser deliveries with purchasing and supplier; bring manuring up to date
Stop manual fertiliser broadcasting (earnings below minimum wage); use semi-mechanised Timac
Keep regular quarterly rat and bagworm census
Plant predator host plants (Cassia:Antigonon:Turnera 60:20:20) in clumps 100–200 m apart
Remove overgrown wild palms and unproductive palms (removal still very minimal)
Maintain drains in flood-prone P07C and P07D
Grade roads from end-May 2026; in future grade in the first half of the year
Finish the 10% tall-palm pruning backlog by June 2026, then rake palm bases
Do not leave harvested bunches or fertiliser bags overnight along the boundary; keep patrols
Monitor worker productivity and earnings to retain skilled workers
Improve crawler and Timac daily productivity
Prune dried fronds in flood-affected C4 and keep monitoring the palms
Address the C3 flooding (sub-drain, topographic survey) raised in Nov 2025
Carry out 2026 leaf sampling as the basis for the 2027 programme
Improve Mix B application quality (some improvements required at C4)
Bait rats if barn owls cannot hold any rise in damage
Complete the whole 2026 fertiliser programme on schedule
Update palm census by drone counting (future programme)
Desilt 110 chains of main drain after the monsoon
Replace genset with solar power (shut down 15 Apr 2026); 2026 capex completed within budget

kb:
LADANG SUNGAI BATU - FACT PACK (Far East Holdings Berhad, Far East group). Manager En. Ahmad Khairul Hakim Bin Mohamad (promoted to Manager January 2026; previously Senior Assistant Manager-in-Charge). Deputy Chief Operating Officer / Plantation Controller En. Nazaruddin Bin Hashim.

SOURCES. (1) Planting Advisory (PA) Report 1/2026, visit 21 May 2026, review period January to April 2026, by Planting Advisor En. Mohd Sufian Bin Yusoff; previous PA visit 20 November 2025 by Tuan Haji Abdullah Bin Busu Hanifah (PA 2/2025, period Jan-Oct 2025). Expenditure checked against the April 2026 progress report. (2) Agronomy Report 1/2026, visit 22 May 2026, by Junior Agronomist En. Ghazali Bin Abd Ghani with Senior Agronomist Mr. Chong Kuan Ming; previous agronomy visit 27 November 2025 (Agro 2/2025, which drew up the 2026 programme). Agro 1/2025 (visit 15 May 2025) holds the 2025 programme.

AREA (PA 1/2026 Table 1, April 2026). Total 906.86 ha; oil palm all mature 886.80 ha (97.79%); building 1.20 ha, vacant 14.76 ha, unplantable 4.10 ha. Fields (ha, SPH): P05A 183.00 (132), P05B 229.10 (123), P07C 257.10 (127), P07D 167.60 (129), P07E 16.70 (111), P12F 33.30 (133); average SPH 127. Planted 2005 (A, B), 2007 (C, D, E), 2012 (F). No replanting planned. Age profile per PA: 4% prime, 96% old mature above 19 years; Agro says 46% old palms (P05A, P05B) and 54% prime 12-19 years. Topography flat to gently rolling, suits mechanisation. Palm census by GPS July 2024: 112,899 palms; drone census planned.

STAFF AND LABOUR (PA, April 2026). Staff: Manager, Chief Clerk Ramlan Bin Mohd Ramli (transferred in January 2026), Account Clerk, two Supervisors - adequate. Workers 68 vs 87 required (-19): harvesting 40 contract vs 44; driver/loader 7 vs 7; weeding 5 vs 7; manuring 10 vs 14; general worker 2 vs 10; mandor 2 vs 3; security 2 vs 2. Ratio 1 worker per 13 ha, harvesters 1 per 22 ha - PA calls labour adequate. Contractors: Wardana harvesting all fields (40 workers); Dyna, S/Kamar, Firdaus drivers/loaders. 16 foreign workers returned from long leave, 3 absconded in 4 months. Agro 1/2026 reports 48 harvesters, a surplus of four, ratio 1:18 ha.

CROP (PA 1/2026 Table 19, Jan-Apr 2026, 886.80 ha). FFB 6,032.05 t vs budget 6,100.00 t (annual budget 20,000.00 t); same period 2025 5,760.75 t; full year 2025 21,774.95 t. Yield 6.80 t/ha vs budget 6.88; same period 2025 6.50; annual budget 22.55; 2025 24.55 t/ha. CPO 1,174.41 t, OER 19.47% (budget 19.30%); kernel 286.52 t, KER 4.75%. Production in line with budget and 5% above last year. By field Jan-Apr 2026 t/ha: P05A 7.29, P05B 6.85, P07C 6.31, P07D 6.82, P07E 5.85 (lowest, low SPH and bunch number), P12F 8.00 (highest, prime age). Bunches per palm 3.06, average bunch weight 17.47 kg. 2026 budget by field t/ha: P05A 23.00, P05B 19.00, P07C 21.40, P07D 27.45, P07E 21.55, P12F 30.00. PA expects the estate to beat 22.55 t/ha.
Five-year yield t/ha (PA Table 21): 2021 18.74, 2022 17.26, 2023 19.85, 2024 23.04, 2025 24.55. Estate tonnes (Agro App 2b): 2019 22,138.71; 2020 22,190.80; 2021 16,621.61; 2022 15,304.00; 2023 17,598.95; 2024 20,429.29; 2025 21,774.95. Monthly 2025: Jan 1,441.80, Feb 1,399.00, Mar 1,418.70, Apr 1,501.25, May 1,512.80, Jun 1,340.80, Jul 1,826.85, Aug 1,983.20, Sep 2,055.35, Oct 2,504.30, Nov 2,524.30, Dec 2,266.60. 2026: Jan 2,034.50, Feb 1,360.05, Mar 1,338.0 (Jan-Mar total printed 4,732.85 t, 5.34 t/ha).
Agro 1/2026: 2025 yield 24.55 t/ha, +6.59% on 2024 (P05A 25.67, P05B 21.79 +19.25%, P07C 24.76, P07D 26.11, P07E 25.36 -16.15%, P12F 27.59 -9.83%). Jan-Mar 2026 +11.11% on Jan-Mar 2025 (Table 16, 4.80 vs 5.23 t/ha); only P07C lower (-1.13%). Jan-Mar 2026 crop 0.8% below estimate. 2025 harvesting rounds 23.50 (97% of target); Jan-Mar 2026 5.93 rounds (99%).

HARVESTING (PA). 40 harvesters with 2 crawlers and 6 Timac; average interval 15 days, 7.93 rounds in Jan-Apr. Productivity 2.14 t per man-day (2,813 man-days); harvesting rate RM38.00/t; earnings RM66.12 to RM88.54 per day (average RM81.32). FFB quality satisfactory, good loose fruit recovery, no ripe bunches left, crop to mill within 24 hours. Mechanisation: crawlers 182.00 ha, 7 harvesters, 7.09 t/machine-day, 2.90 t/harvester-day; Timac 704.80 ha, 27 harvesters, 10.16 and 2.68 t/day - machine output a bit low. Agro: intervals 13-17 days, no crop backlog, minimal over-ripe bunches, loose fruit well collected; crawlers 6.79 t/machine-day, Mechanical Badang 8.98.

COST (PA 1/2026 Table 23, Jan-Apr 2026, RM per t FFB, actual vs budget): general charges 73.92 vs 95.75; upkeep and cultivation 94.06 vs 115.27; harvesting and collection 81.28 vs 81.53; total ex-estate 249.26 vs 292.54 (15% below; annual budget 274.58). Per t CPO 1,280.27 vs 1,520.02. Underspend: general charges in worker incentives and recruitment; upkeep from late fertiliser. General charges RM502.83/ha vs RM658.60 (24% lower); overspent items: executive salaries +7% (manager promotion), non-executive salaries +17% (new chief clerk), staff medical +131%, labour medical +90% (two-week hospital stay), welfare +7%, labour electricity +18% (genset diesel), water +7%, quarters upkeep +17% (roof repairs), work permit renewal +11%. Upkeep RM/ha to date vs budget: weeding 104.21 vs 86.68 (+20%, follow-up round from 2025); manuring 340.78 vs 520.19 (-34%); pest and disease 24.41 vs 31.21; census 2.92 vs 4.33; drains 22.02 vs 16.77; roads 71.21 vs 70.82; boundaries 4.93 vs 4.67; pruning 69.32 vs 58.19 (+19%, corrective pruning); total 639.80 vs 792.87. Harvesting RM52.33/t, internal transport RM28.62/t, supervision RM0.33/t. PA 2/2025 (Jan-Oct 2025): cost RM246.51/t vs budget 274.05.

MANURING. 2025: whole programme applied, 1,223.90 t (Mix B 510.40, Mix C 482.20, kieserite 60.70, RP 170.60). 2026 to April (PA Table 10): Jan Mix B 191.30 t completed; Feb Mix B 62.25 t completed; Mar RP 127.65 t (85.50 delivered, 37.50 applied); Apr Mix C 170.20, May Mix C 55.35, Jun RP 41.50 not delivered. 291.05 t applied = 53% of 551.40 t due by April; delay from late delivery of RP and Mixture C; estate to expedite with purchasing. Semi-mechanised Timac application 40 bags/day, RM80.00/day; manual 25 bags/day, RM60.00/day, below minimum wage - stop manual. Agro (as at March): 19% of first half, 11% of the year (1,127.35 t); Mix B check in P07C4 acceptable with some improvements needed; no EFB or POME applied in 2025-2026.
2026 programme (Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1, g per palm): P05A, P05B, P07C - Mix B 2,250 Jan, 2,000 Apr, 2,250 Jul, 2,000 Oct, plus RP 1,500 in March for A2, A3 and all of P07C. P07D, P07E - Mix B 2,250 Feb, 2,000 May, 2,250 Aug, 2,000 Nov, RP 1,500 Jun. P12F - Mix B 2,250 in Feb, May, Aug and Nov, RP 1,500 Jun. 2027 programme to be drawn up after the second-half visit. 2025 programme (Agro 1/2025): P05A/B Mix B 2,250 Feb, Mix C 2,000 May, Mix B 2,250 Jul, RP 1,500 Aug, Mix C 2,000 Oct; P07C/D/E Mix B 2,250 Jan, kieserite 1,000 Mar, Mix C 2,250 Apr, RP 1,500 Jun, Mix B 2,250 Jul, Mix C 2,250 Oct; P12F same with Mix B 2,500 and RP 1,750.

WEEDING. PA: one round of circle and selective spraying done in all fields to April; circles mostly clean, little woody growth; cut frond butts and debris need raking; sporadic half-dead Clidemia (dosage or rain) and tough jungle woodies need spot-spraying; glyphosate within 2 m, triclopyr selective; premix solution under supervisor. Sprayers 6.50 and 5.50 ha/day, RM71.50 and RM82.50/day. Agro: 2025 three inter-row rounds done, final circle round over 90%; 2026 inter-row round 1 71% at March, circle 54% at April; only 4 of 7 weeding workers; soft grasses dominate; broadleaf weeds controlled in E1, C3, A2.

PESTS AND DISEASES. Rat damage March 2026: P05A 3%, P05B 2%, P07C 2%, P07D 1%, P07E 1%, P12 2% - insignificant. One round of Arakus (brodifacoum) baiting in all fields. 82 barn owl nests (1 per 11 ha), 81 occupied (PA 95%, Agro table 99%). Predator host plants 2,120 chains planted (60 chains in 2026 vs 1,030 programmed). No leaf-eating pest outbreak; Ganoderma negligible (Nov 2025 census: P05A 4, P05B 6, P07C 8, P07D 11, P07E 2 palms).

PRUNING. Round 1 done on all 886.80 ha; about 10% of tall palm area still removing hanging dry fronds, backlog from high crop in late 2025, to finish by June 2026 then rake palm bases. Standard satisfactory. Agro: pruning and sanitation rated good in every sub-block; 2025 had three rounds with no backlog.

NUTRITION AND FIELD. Palms green to dark green. Sub-block C4 flooded October 2025 (receded in 2-3 weeks): mild nitrogen deficiency, reduced canopy, dried fronds to prune. Mild K and boron deficiency in A3 and C2. 2025 leaf analysis (May 2025): N and Mg below optimum in several blocks (N deficient A2, C4; Mg deficient A3, C2, C3, C4, D1, D2, D3, E1; B marginal A3, C2, D3). New leaf sampling in 2026 for the 2027 programme. Agro 2/2025: about 60 palms in C3 flooded from 20 October 2025, sub-drain and topographic survey recommended.

ROADS, DRAINS, SECURITY, CAPEX. 110 chains of main drain (8x6x4 ft) desilted after the monsoon; P07C and P07D flood-prone. Roads passable; 86 t crusher run and 360 backhoe hours; grading planned end-May 2026 (could not grade in 2025 due to wet weather). Boundary with private estates and smallholders: patrols in place; bunches and fertiliser bags not to be left overnight. 2026 capex RM719,252.50 vs RM716,000.00 budget: Toyota Hilux RM148,252.50 (2% over), solar plant RM446,000 (genset shut down 15 April 2026), store roof RM80,000, changing room and chemical mixing RM45,000. John Deere tractor running cost RM8.59/hr vs RM4.08 (clutch repair RM3,995.00).

RAINFALL. Five-year average 3,650 mm over 150 days, mostly October-January. Annual totals (PA App 1): 2022 4,007.5 mm/193 days; 2023 3,364.0/159; 2024 2,989.0/109; 2025 4,407 mm/140 days; Jan-Apr 2026 347 mm/22 days.

KEY ADVICE. Premix herbicide and check dosage; rake palm circles; spot-spray woodies; expedite fertiliser delivery and stop manual application; quarterly rat/bagworm census; plant beneficial plants; remove wild palms; keep drains in P07C/P07D; grade roads early; clear pruning backlog by June; keep boundary security; improve machine productivity; treat C4 flood area; leaf sampling 2026; finish the 2026 programme on schedule.
